newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industry on rollercoaster ride to nowhere.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industry on rollercoaster ride to nowhere.

text.p: Brazilian industrial output is lurching between monthly highs and lows but is effectively stuck at more or less current levels, the private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said Tuesday.

Output in seasonally adjusted terms fell 2.35 percent in February from January, after a month-on-month increase of 3.9 percent in January and a 4.4 percent drop in December, according to numbers published by the CNI.

"What we may be seeing is a stabilizing of the economy at current levels, but it is early to say what will happen in the next few months," Jose Guilherme dos Reis, the head of the CNI's economic department.
The confederation's president Fernando Bezerra said he could definitely draw at least one conclusion from the numbers, however.
"There is no overheating of the economy as has sometimes been suggested and therefore there is no need for any measures to brake growth," Bezerra told reporters at a news conference.
Industrial sales in the first two months of the year were 6.49 percent higher than in the same period last year, according to CNI data.
But dos Reis said that growth should be seen in the context of low output during the first half of last year, before the government decided to relax a series of controls on credit.
Furthermore, February's 4.82 percent drop in industry sales in real terms, excluding seasonal factors, was the biggest fall for that month since the CNI began measuring sales in 1992.
One explanation for the contrasting sales figures in recent months may be the availability of consumer credit which fuelled growth in industrial output throughout 1996, he said.
"People have been changing their buying habits because credit is generally available and they don't have to wait for their year-end bonuses before spending," dos Reis said.
But rising levels of bad debt showed consumer-led growth was likely to fizzle out soon. "Bad debt will have its toll (on growth). Families have reached their debt limits," he said.
On a more positive note, an expected bumper harvest this year, combined with high prices for agricultural products, should boost industry sales, particularly in the third quarter.
